title: 第三发之后
short: The guard fires three shots before reloading. During the reload, it steps back and cannot fire. Stay behind cover until the third shot, then move sideways and attack. The red barrel can hurt anyone nearby, including you. Keep your distance before you shoot it.
long: The outpost guard looks dangerous, but its weapon has a limit. It fires three shots before it must reload. During that pause, the guard steps back and cannot fire. You can use a crate as cover while counting the shots. After the third one, move sideways to find a clear angle. A red fuel barrel stands near the enemy position. Destroying it can damage nearby guards, but the blast can hurt you too. This is a chance to change the fight without standing in the open. The important thing is to notice the pause and choose your moment.
zh: 守卫射击三次后必须换弹。换弹时会后退，无法开火。先借掩体躲过三发，再横向移动寻找射击角度。红色油桶爆炸会伤及附近所有人，也包括你。保持距离再引爆。
question: 最适合离开掩体反击的时机是？
options: 守卫第三发之后，开始换弹时
explain: before reloading 表示射完三发才换弹；during the reload 是它无法开火的空档。
sentence: Wait for the reload before we attack.
sentence_zh: 等对手换弹，我们再进攻。

title: 修通的侧路
short: The central bridge is the shortest route, but the guards can watch it easily. A second crossing lies to the east. Once you repair it, you can approach from the side. The new route does not remove the enemy. It gives you another angle and a choice.
long: A narrow bridge connects the camp to the outpost. It is a quick route, but it also puts you directly in front of the guards. The broken crossing to the east could offer a different approach. Repairing it requires timber from a completed fight. Once the work is finished, the crossing stays open. On later visits, you can reach the outpost from the side and make the guards turn away from their original position. The bridge does not make your weapon stronger or guarantee a victory. Its value is the extra choice: you can change where the fight begins.
zh: 中间的桥很近，但容易被守卫盯住。修好东边的栈桥后，可以从侧翼接近据点。修桥不会消灭敌人，也不保证取胜，它给你新的角度和选择。侧桥建成后会一直保留。
question: 侧桥最大的作用是什么？
options: 让武器自动造成更多伤害
explain: another angle and a choice 指新的进攻角度与选择，收益来自空间变化。
sentence: We can approach the outpost from the side.
sentence_zh: 我们可以从侧面接近据点。

title: 别追得太急
short: The red raider likes to chase. If you run straight away, it will follow. Use a solid rock to break its line of sight, then change direction. It must search for you before it can aim again. A retreat can create an opening, but running blindly into the river will not help.
long: The red raider is more willing to chase than the other guards. Its speed can make you feel rushed, but the pursuit also creates an opportunity. A solid rock blocks both bullets and the raider's view. If you move behind it and turn, the enemy must search for your new position. Watch where it expects you to appear. You may be able to attack from a different angle while it is turning. Retreating is useful when it changes the situation. Simply running in a straight line gives the pursuer an easy path and may lead you toward an unbuilt crossing.
zh: 红色急进者喜欢追击。借岩石打断它的视线，再改变方向，让它重新搜索你的所在。撤退要能改变局面；一直直线后退容易被追上，或被河道挡住。
question: 为什么绕到岩石后再转向有用？
options: 所有敌人都会立刻逃跑
敌人暂时失去视线，需要重新找你
explain: break its line of sight 是打断视线，随后敌人需要搜索。
sentence: Use the rock to break its line of sight.
sentence_zh: 利用岩石打断它的视线。

title: 会绕行的对手
short: The purple guard does not always move straight toward you. It tries to find an angle beside your cover. If you stare only at the closest enemy, you may miss it. Move before both guards can fire from different directions. Your dash can carry you through a bullet, but it needs time to recover.
long: Two guards can be more dangerous than one even when their weapons are the same. The purple guard looks for a route beside your cover instead of always following the shortest path. Meanwhile, another guard may keep your attention in front. When their firing angles separate, a single crate may no longer protect you from both. Check the sides and move before the situation becomes difficult. A well-timed dash briefly protects you as you cross a bullet's path. However, the dash needs time to recover. Spending it too early can leave you without a way out when the second guard arrives.
zh: 紫色守卫会寻找你掩体的侧面。注意两名敌人是否形成不同射线，及时换位。闪避可以短暂穿过弹幕，但需要恢复时间，太早使用可能在真正危险时没有退路。
question: 什么时候一只木箱可能保护不了你？
options: 两名敌人从不同角度开火时
敌人都在同一方向换弹时
explain: different directions 指不同方向。侧面敌人会绕过原先遮挡射线的掩体。
sentence: Move before the second guard reaches our side.
sentence_zh: 在第二名守卫绕到侧面之前移动。

title: 留住一个掩体
short: A wooden crate blocks bullets, but enough hits will destroy it. Breaking the enemy's cover may give you a clear shot. Breaking your own cover may leave you exposed. Before firing at a crate, check who is using it. A useful object can become a problem when the positions change.
long: You notice a wooden crate between two firing positions. At first, it seems like an obstacle that should be removed. Yet its value depends on who is standing behind it. When an enemy uses the crate, destroying it opens a path for your next shot. When you need it to block incoming bullets, destroying it removes your own protection. The same object can help either side as the fight moves around the outpost. Before shooting, look at the positions rather than treating every breakable object as a target. Keeping one piece of cover may give you the time needed to reload safely.
zh: 木箱可以挡子弹，也会被打坏。打破敌人的掩体可能创造机会，但打破自己的掩体会让你暴露。判断谁正在使用它，再决定是否破坏。保留一个掩体能帮助你安全换弹。
question: 文中建议开火前先判断什么？
explain: check who is using it 提醒你判断掩体当前保护谁，而非见到可破坏物就开火。
sentence: Keep some cover so we can reload safely.
sentence_zh: 留下一些掩体，方便我们安全换弹。

title: 有计划地重来
short: After a failed attack, look for one decision you can change. Perhaps you left cover before the guard reloaded. Perhaps you used your dash before you needed it. Try one different approach on the next run. A useful lesson explains what happened and suggests an action you can test.
long: A failed attack can feel like wasted effort, especially when the same mistake happens twice. Instead of changing everything at once, choose one decision to examine. Did you leave cover while the guard still had ammunition? Did you chase an enemy into a second firing line? Or did you spend your dash before the dangerous moment? Pick one explanation and test a different action on the next run. The result may support your idea or show that you missed something. Progress becomes easier to notice when you can connect an outcome to a choice you made. That is more useful than simply deciding that you are bad at the game.
zh: 失败之后，找一个可以改变的决定：是否太早离开掩体，追进了第二条射线，或提前用掉闪避？下一场先测试一种不同做法，把结果与自己的选择联系起来。
question: 复盘后最值得尝试的做法是？
options: 完全忽略上一次的经历
选一个具体决定，测试不同做法
explain: Try one different approach 表示有针对性地换一种做法，验证自己对失败原因的判断。
sentence: Try a different approach on the next run.
sentence_zh: 下一次尝试一种不同的做法。
